frames.observation: The exact custom middle body is readable in settled native snowman_idle. The faceted torso, articulated arms and crystal hands form a coherent center between the base, scarf and head without a sampled gap or mesh explosion.
A later idle sample preserves the compact torso and symmetric arm placement. The hands retain their separate crystal-finger shapes while the complete five-part silhouette remains assembled.

At the telemetry-selected native Attack trigger, the torso turns with the upper stack and both arms begin snowman_attack1 from coherent shoulders. The exact body remains fully readable above the base.

During native snowman_attack1, the chest remains compact while the articulated arms and hands follow the pose. Bright ice particles overlap some edges, but no obvious stretch, detachment or collapse is visible.
The ordinary zero-focus attack begins with Rimecrown intact at HP58. The exact middle body remains aligned between the base and head before the native hero action resolves.

During native attack-slot resolution, the torso, arms and crystal hands remain readable in the complete stacked silhouette. This precedes the measured HP transition and does not by itself establish hit motion.

The telemetry-selected native Damaged trigger coincides with a bright impact sphere and foreground hero. The middle body remains visible behind them, while the glow prevents fine inspection of the chest and near arm.

The recorded 8-damage label is visible during native snowman_damage. The head lifts above the torso while the chest, arms and hands separate in their animated poses without a long deformation. Smoke and the hero obscure part of the center.

After the ordinary damage reaction, the exact middle body is reassembled between the base and head at HP50. Camera afterimages limit edge inspection, but the torso and arms retain their intended proportions.
The capture ends during another native attack with both arms extended from the compact torso. The visible body and hands remain coherent while the native effect reports Fizzle over the target.

The explicit KillSingle capture begins with the exact middle body and complete Rimecrown intact at HP50. The ordinary hero UI remains visible, but this action is a separate fixture rather than ordinary lethal gameplay.

At the exact native Death trigger, the middle body remains assembled beneath the head behind the large impact effect. The glow prevents fine surface judgment, so this frame primarily establishes action provenance and pre-separation alignment.

Native snowman_deathDirect is underway with the recorded 1000-damage label. Body parts travel upward through smoke while the base remains behind. This is an animated fall-apart sequence, not ragdoll behavior.

The upper assembly has moved through the foreground and is mostly hidden by the hero and smoke while the base remains at the target. Visible crystal points retain their shape, but this frame cannot establish complete body placement or collision.

A small separated upper assembly is visible far beyond the persistent base near the rear doorway. Distance, blur and foreground overlap prevent a reliable middle-body surface or resting-placement judgment.

The native loot panel and foreground hero block the middle body's last observed area. Exact telemetry still reports the renderer active, enabled, visible and identity-stable, but this image cannot establish a readable corpse or body surface.

At the end of the complete 120-frame capture, the loot panel still blocks the target and middle-body area. Exact telemetry remains stable, but this handoff does not establish later corpse lifetime, cleanup causality or final disposal.

requirements: All 17 referenced original PNGs were inspected before assigning the reviewed status.
Every observation is scoped to the exact frame and its telemetry boundary.
The ordinary 58 to 50 hit is separate from the explicit 50 to 0 KillSingle fixture.
The source reports m_DoRagdoll false and zero rigidbodies, so the observed fall-apart death is animated and receives no ragdoll credit.

Exact middle-body instance, owner, mesh and bone signature remain unchanged while active, enabled and visible in all 360 retained telemetry frames; exact collision, corpse lifetime and final cleanup remain unproven.
